recipes.name: Coconut Milk Corned Beef and Cabbage
ingredients_raw: 2 stalks celery, cut into large chunks
2 carrots, peeled and cut into large chunks
1 pound potatoes, peeled and cut into large chunks
0.5 small head cabbage, cored and cut into large chunks

steps.text: Place brisket, fat-side up, in the bottom of a Dutch oven. Stir in water, coconut milk, tomato paste, fish sauce, red curry paste, coriander, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam that accumulates.
Stir in onion, celery, and carrots. Bring mixture to a boil; reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 3 hours, turning once.

Stir in potatoes and cabbage; cook until potatoes are tender and cabbage is soft and sweet, about 35 minutes. Transfer beef to a plate; thinly slice across the grain. Ladle potato cabbage mixture into bowls and top with sliced beef.

raw_recipe.headline: Coconut Milk Corned Beef and Cabbage
raw_recipe.description: In Chef John's novel twist on an old classic, corned beef and cabbage is braised in coconut milk, giving it a subtle sweetness and richness that is delightful.

review.reviewBody: My wife is from Thailand so we know the flavors. We were mixed as to whether to even try this because I didn't want to waste a corned beef if the flavors were too "conflicted". On the other hand, the "same old" corn beef and cabbage IS kind of boring. WOW was this good. The ammounts of coconut milk and curry paste were just enough to "hint" at the changed recipe and there was a richness in the broth that we both loved. Only change I made was to use a crock pot instead of a dutch oven. Now my wife and I are talking about whether to "push" the coconut milk and curry to make them a little more prominent. We LOVED this as written and I recommend this as a change. It is NOT radical nor conflicted at the table. thanks rc

10 stars and absolutely AMAZING!! I used veg broth vs water and used TBLS red curry paste. Just wow! Hearty but fantastic flavor and texture combination! would absolutely make again! Another home run recipe Chef John!
Delicious. The cabbage and broth is delicious by itself. Smooth, tasty. No other seasonings needed. I used curry powder as I didn't have paste, and I don't like spicy. TY.

Great--just had some leftovers for lunch today. As other reviewers mentioned, the coconut milk adds a level of richness and the bit of red curry paste is just enough for interest without overpowering other flavors. Such a great twist on corned beef!
The best Corned Beef and Cabbage.

Amazing that just a few ingredients can make such a basic dish so delicious. I haven't made corned beef any other way since 2017. I definitely double up the Curry paste and throw in a little more coconut milk and veggies.
I've done it in the crock pot and on the stove. I think the crock pot is much less hassle. But it can be tough to fit everything into the pot. 
The first time I prepped it, I shared the recipe with a good friend. She thanks me every year on St. Patrick's Day!

I read the reviews first, I’m glad I did. I too added 10x the red curry paste and one extra can of coconut milk in place of some of the water. Was very flavorful and came out very pretty when played. Will be sharing this recipe.

Have done this recipe 8 times now with absolutely fantastic reviews each and every time from all whom have devoured this feast. I triple the ingredients as always cook for large groups. Well done thanks for the recipe it is my best corned beef by far.
Excellent! I always buy four or five corned beefs every March. I love having a new easy recipe that is delicious! I used the instant pot for 70mins on high pressure. Excellent!

Yesterday was St. Patrick's Day. I was asked to do Corned Beef and Cabbage for the Elks Lodge. I used your recipe for Coconut milk corned beef. I cooked 18+ lbs. of brisket & I should have doubled that. I have never gotten raves like that before & I've been cooking most of my 74 years.
One word, “GOOD”! I followed this recipe exactly!
Great recipe! Only suggestion is to cut the cabbage into smaller bite sized pieces.
